simple.meaning: מַעֲבָר (maʻăbâr) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a crossing -place (of a river, a ford ; of a mountain, a pass ); abstractly, a transit , i.e. (figuratively) overwhelming.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 11 times across Genesis, Joshua, Judges, 1 Samuel, Isaiah, and 1 more, beginning at Genesis 32:23. Its contexts include family line, death.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַעֲבָר (H4569).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

definitions.short: a crossing -place (of a river, a ford ; of a mountain, a pass ); abstractly, a transit , i.e. (figuratively) overwhelming
definitions.full: H4569. ma 'abar [ מַעֲבָר ] noun [masculine] ford, pass, passing ; — only construct: 1 יַבֹּק מַעֲבַר Gen 32:23 (J) the ford of (the) Jabbok . 2 pass , מִכְמָשׂ מַעֲבַר 1Sam 13:23 the pass of M . 3 passing, sweep , מַטֶּה כָּלמַֿעֲבַר Isa 30:32 every sweep of the rod ( עָבַר 4c ). מַעְבָּרָה noun feminine ford, pass, passage ; — absolute ׳מ Isa 10:29 ; plural מַעְבָּרוֺת 16:2 ; Jer 51:32 , מַעְבְּרוֺת absolute Josh 2:7 ; 1Sam 14:4 ; construct Judg 3:28 2 t.; — 1 ford , only plural Josh 2:7 (JE), Judg 3:28 ; 12:5-6 , Isa 16:2 ; so also 1Sam 13:7 (for עָֽבְרוּ ᵑ0 ) We Dr Kit Löhr; + מַעְבֶּרֶת 1Kin 7:46 2Chr 4:17 , see סֻכּוֺת 2 pass (wady, ravine), 1Sam 14:4 ; Isa 10:29 . 3 passage in defensive works of Babylonian Jer 51:32 .

occurrences.englishText: He took them, and sent them over the stream, and sent over that which he had.
The men pursued them along the way to the fords of the Jordan River. As soon as those who pursued them had gone out, they shut the gate.

He said to them, “Follow me; for Yahweh has delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand.” They followed him, and took the fords of the Jordan against the Moabites, and didn’t allow any man to pass over.
The Gileadites took the fords of the Jordan against the Ephraimites. Whenever a fugitive of Ephraim said, “Let me go over,” the men of Gilead said to him, “Are you an Ephraimite?” If he said, “No;”

then they said to him, “Now say ‘Shibboleth;’ ” and he said “Sibboleth”; for he couldn’t manage to pronounce it correctly, then they seized him and killed him at the fords of the Jordan. At that time, forty-two thousand of Ephraim fell.
The garrison of the Philistines went out to the pass of Michmash.

Between the passes, by which Jonathan sought to go over to the Philistines’ garrison, there was a rocky crag on the one side, and a rocky crag on the other side: and the name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh.
They have gone over the pass. They have taken up their lodging at Geba. Ramah trembles. Gibeah of Saul has fled.
For it will be that as wandering birds, as a scattered nest, so will the daughters of Moab be at the fords of the Arnon.
Every stroke of the rod of punishment, which Yahweh will lay on him, will be with the sound of tambourines and harps. He will fight with them in battles, brandishing weapons.
